sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Patch/FRAP assay: HA- and myc-tagged ENG co-expressed at COS7 cell surface; lateral diffusion and homo-oligomerization measured and reported as functional — tagged receptors participated normally in oligomerization studies.
sites.rationale: ENG (UniProt P17813) is a type I single-pass transmembrane protein: signal peptide residues 1–25, large ectodomain 26–591, TM 592–614, intracellular tail 615–658. The tag is described as extracellular in all three ledger lines; the only extracellular terminus is the mature N-terminus beginning at residue 26. Therefore insert_after_residue = 25 (last residue of the signal peptide, A), placing the tag immediately before E26 — the canonical topology-derived junction. Python verification confirms seq[24]='A' and seq[25]='E'. L2 (PMC10799020) and L3 (PMC8916587) independently corroborate the same construct and position. Full-length ENG carrying HA or myc epitope tags was expressed at the surface of COS7 cells; patch/FRAP experiments confirmed surface display and were used to study ENG homo-oligomerization. The tag is described as extracellular; ENG is a type I TM protein with a single extracellular terminus (mature N-terminus, residue 26) and a single intracellular C-terminus — no residue number is stated in the paper.

sources.claim: To study endoglin homo-oligomerization, we coexpressed hemagglutinin (HA)- or myc-tagged endoglin at the surface of COS7 cells and conducted patch/FRAP studies on the tagged receptors.

literature_notes: All three ledger lines (L1, L2, L3) describe HA- or myc-tagged full-length ENG with an extracellular tag but none specifies an insertion residue number. ENG has exactly one extracellular terminus (mature N-terminus, residue 26), making the topology-derived junction unambiguous: insert_after_residue = 25. L1 was chosen as the primary supporting clip because it provides the highest validation level (surface display by patch/FRAP + oligomerization function measured). L2 (PMC10799020) explicitly uses the phrase 'extracellular epitope tag' and confirms the same surface-and-function level; L3 (PMC8916587) confirms expression of HA-tagged ENG in HEK293 cells but the clip does not state surface display or functional outcome. The missense variants P165L and V105D mentioned in L3 are disease-associated substitutions used as experimental comparators, not tag insertion sites, and are not promoted to sites. No ledger line names an internal loop insertion or a C-terminal (intracellular) tag for ENG.
